links.outcome: Reproducibility of diagnostic accuracy on repeated readings of the same images
links.effect: Diagnostic accuracy declined by up to 30% when 20 images were re-read after 30 and 90 days and was unrelated to self-reported confidence (Spearman's rho = 0.117, p = 0.776).
links.quote: Diagnostic accuracy declined by up to 30% when 20 images were re-read after 30 and 90 days and seemed unrelated to the tool's self-reported confidence (Spearman's ρ = 0.117 (p = 0.776)).

links.effect: Diagnostic accuracy seemed unrelated to the tool's self-reported confidence (Spearman's rho = 0.117, p = 0.776).

links.outcome: Fabricated imaging findings and misidentified modalities/regions in GPT-4V responses
links.effect: The tool fabricated 258 imaging findings in 412 responses and misidentified imaging modalities or anatomic regions in 65 images.
links.quote: While the described imaging findings matched the suggested diagnoses in 92.7%, indicating valid diagnostic reasoning, the tool fabricated 258 imaging findings in 412 responses and misidentified imaging modalities or anatomic regions in 65 images.

links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of autonomous GPT-4V radiologic image interpretation
links.effect: Accuracy was 8.3% uncontextualized, 29.1% contextualized first diagnosis, and 63.6% with correct diagnosis among differentials.
links.quote: With its pronounced propensity to favor context over image information, the tool's diagnostic accuracy improved from 8.3% (uncontextualized) to 29.1% (contextualized, first diagnosis correct) and 63.6% (contextualized, correct diagnosis among differential diagnoses) (p ≤ 0.001, Cochran's Q test).
